posts.author: Kaff 📊
posts.text:
One thing crypto has taught me is that buying a good project and making money from its token are two completely different things.

You can spend weeks researching a protocol with growing revenue, billions in TVL, a product that's clearly better than competitors, and still watch its token bleed for months.

Meanwhile, some coin with half the fundamentals ends up outperforming everything.

Bc the market doesn't reward a project simply for being good. It rewards the gap between what people expect today and what they're willing to believe tomorrow.

And that's why I think buying a strong, underappreciated thesis can be far more profitable than simply buying strong fundamentals.

Look at $AAVE vs $HYPE.

– Aave is one of the strongest businesses in DeFi, yet $AAVE is down 25% YTD.

– $HYPE is up around 170% YTD, despite the broader market struggling.

One has a successful protocol. The other has a mechanism that makes protocol success matter directly to the token.

I think that's where a lot of fundamental investors get trapped.

They spend so much time proving a project is undervalued based on its revenue, TVL or adoption that they forget to ask who's actually going to buy the token next.

Cheap can stay cheap for a very long time.

Flip that around, imagine a project that looks mediocre today, but you notice something the market hasn't properly priced in yet.

Maybe a product is gaining traction, a fee switch is about to change token economics, a new source of demand is forming, or capital is starting to rotate into a sector nobody cared about.

The opportunity is in how much the market's expectations could change once that thesis starts playing out.

Crypto makes this especially interesting because attention itself can become a source of liquidity.

A thesis starts with a small group of believers.

Then the data starts supporting it, more people notice, new buyers come in, price moves, and suddenly the same thesis that sounded ridiculous a few months ago becomes obvious.

By the time everyone agrees, a good chunk of the repricing has already happened.

But that doesn't mean buying whatever narrative is trending. We've seen enough AI, DePIN and memes pump on a good story only to give everything back once attention rotates.

The interesting part is finding where an underappreciated thesis meets improving fundamentals, actual token demand, and a catalyst that can change the market's mind.

There's another detail I think gets overlooked.

A thesis can be right and still be a terrible trade if it's already crowded.

If everyone is positioned for the same outcome, who is left to buy when the good news finally arrives?

That's probably why some of the safest-looking fundamental plays end up being dead money, while the uncomfortable trades nobody wants to touch produce the biggest returns.

@DWFLabs found that 13 of 15 tokens with active or announced value-accrual mechanisms outperformed BTC YTD in its sample.

It says something about where capital has become more selective. So I've been thinking about crypto investing a little differently.

Instead of just asking whether a project has strong fundamentals, I'd rather understand what the market currently believes, what it might be missing, what could force that belief to change.

Because fundamentals tell you how good a project is today. A thesis tells you why the market might value it differently tomorrow.

The biggest asymmetry usually comes when you understand that difference before the rest of the market does.

posts.text: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director. NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it. The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries. Global contacts for media inquiries. Newsroom updates delivered to your inbox.

posts.text: Live updates: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia | CNN Business. Live Updates The stunning reversal by the board has turbocharged an already buoyant day for US stocks. Two CEOs of some of the largest artificial intelligence companies commented on Jensen Huang’s reinstatement Monday. The mistake has been corrected,” Elon Musk posted on X, his social media site. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman simply posted “Jensen!” on X. Musk, who is the CEO of Grok chatbot maker xAI, previously advocated for Huang’s reinstatement, going so far as to sign a petition for Huang’s reinstatement alongside shareholders and other company heads. President Donald Trump said that he believes his intervention in the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO was “very important.” “I believe my intervention was very important,” Trump told CNBC in a phone interview, adding that it came in consultation with other top advisers, including Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “I worked with other people, you know, in the administration – JD, Scott, and you know, and Howard. By the way, Howard Lutnick was very good. Very, he’s very professional,” Trump said. “I call them the opposites, Scott and Howard.” Bessent and Lutnick had clashed in the past over issues related to Nvidia – with Bessent notably confronting Lutnick for not labeling Nvidia customer Megaspeed a national security threat. President Donald Trump downplayed the prospect of Republican blowback over his push for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, expressing confidence that the party “will come around.” “When I speak to them, they’re going to be great,” Trump told CNBC. “Republicans will come around.” The president’s remarks came despite a bipartisan push in recent weeks to investigate Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence, as well as Trump administration decision-making that may have allowed Nvidia’s advanced chips to be diverted to China . Huang is slated to give closed-door testimony on Capitol Hill in early December, following demands from the Republicans in charge of a trio of House committees. Federal authorities have been investigating Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was an executive, since 2024 over whether it was in violation of export controls, the Justice and Commerce departments announced last week . As part of the investigation, authorities interviewed Alice Huang, the businesswoman who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The US intelligence community is also working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with the Chinese government, CNN reported earlier this month, citing sources. In last week’s joint statement, the agencies said the Commerce Department first began the investigation after “identifying suspicious activity” while monitoring for possible semiconductor diversion — the unlawful rerouting of restricted computer chips. The department’s investigators asked Nvidia for records of its sales to Megaspeed. Subsequently, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its no sell list, according to the statement. The Justice Department has since taken “the lead role” in a criminal investigation of the company, the statement said. President Donald Trump said Monday that he didn’t press Chinese leader Xi Jingping on ties Alice Huang may have had to the country’s government during their meeting last week. “I didn’t discuss that,” Trump told CNBC in a phone call Monday morning. “No, I didn’t, I assume he knew the young lady.” The president added that Xi told him that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was “a genius,” and mused repeatedly throughout the interview that China may have sought to recruit Huang if he weren’t reinstated atop Nvidia. Trump’s decision not to ask Xi about Alice Huang, who had an extramarital affair with Jensen Huang, came despite suspicions she had ties to Chinese intelligence. Trump on Monday also dismissed a New York Times report that Alice Huang had been in direct contact with China’s spy agency. “He’s at a very high level, I don’t think he knows that,” Trump said of Xi’s knowledge of Alice Huang. “I didn’t get into that kind of detail.” President Donald Trump argued once again this morning that he doesn’t believe the woman that Jensen Huang had an affair with is a Chinese spy, and said that even if advanced Nvidia chips were sold to China, it wouldn’t necessarily be Huang’s fault. “As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy … But with Jensen, I don’t believe that’s true,” Trump told CNBC during an interview on Monday shortly after Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia. CNN previously reported that there are questions within the intelligence community about whether Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman involved with Jensen Huang, was actually a spy, though some officials believe she posed a clear counterintelligence risk. Trump continued to defend his close ally Jensen Huang in the CNBC interview this morning, saying Huang wouldn’t “necessarily” be responsible if advanced chips were diverted to China. “But if they sold to the company that she is with and you know, that would be standard. If they then took it and, you know, gave it to China, that wouldn’t be standard, but that wouldn’t necessarily and probably wouldn’t be — because I don’t think he’d do it — that wouldn’t be Jensen’s fault,” Trump told CNBC. Federal agents had interviewed Alice Huang in 2025 as part of an investigation into possible export control violations. Nvidia’s GTC conference, which takes place in Washington D.C. from Nov. 30 to Dec. 3, will be the company’s first major live event since Huang’s resignation and reinstatement as CEO. During the conference, Nvidia usually details its new technologies, which can range from chips to new models and tools for developers. Huang typically anchors the event with a keynote outlining his vision and announcing the company’s new offerings. Nv

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board on Monday announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) also climbed more than 30%. In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO > "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO," he added. Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. Just last week, Jones told investors during the company's Q3 earnings call that Nvidia had no plans to bring back Huang. Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 after an alleged affair with Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang admitted to having an affair at the time but didn't name the woman. He also allegedly had affairs with two Nvidia employees, including executive Kimberly Powell. Alice Huang was the executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling high-powered Nvidia chips to China. The company said the board received input from senior levels of the US government and, based on that input, doesn't believe Huang's reinstatement poses a national security risk. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry, and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work," he added. Jensen Huang's allies, including President Trump, reportedly lobbied for his return as CEO. In a Truth Social post, Trump lauded Huang's reinstatement. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Trump said. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," Trump continued, adding he considers Huang a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." posts.text: Thông cáo báo chí về tình hình lao động, việc làm quý III và 9 tháng năm 2026. Thị trường lao động chín tháng năm 2026 khả quan. Quy mô lực lượng lao động, số người có việc làm và thu nhập bình quân của người lao động đều tăng so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp duy trì ở mức 2,22%; tỷ lệ thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động là 1,53%, thấp hơn so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Kết quả đạt được phản ánh nhu cầu lao động và hoạt động sản xuất, kinh doanh tiếp tục được cải thiện. a) Lực lượng lao động Lực lượng lao động từ 15 tuổi trở lên của cả nước quý III/2026 ước đạt 54,1 triệu người, cao hơn 278,4 nghìn người so với quý trước và cao hơn 709,7 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước; tỷ lệ tham gia lực lượng lao động là 68,5%, cao hơn 0,1 điểm phần trăm so với quý trước nhưng thấp hơn 0,1 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tính chung chín tháng năm 2026, lực lượng lao động từ 15 tuổi trở lên là 53,8 triệu người, cao hơn 697,0 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tỷ lệ lao động qua đào tạo có bằng, chứng chỉ quý III/2026 là 30,4%, cao hơn 0,6 điểm phần trăm so với quý trước và cao hơn 1,1 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tính chung chín tháng năm 2026, tỷ lệ lao động qua đào tạo có bằng, chứng chỉ là 29,9%, cao hơn 0,8 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước, cho thấy chất lượng nguồn lao động ngày càng được cải thiện. b) Lao động có việc làm Lao động có việc làm quý III/2026 đạt gần 53,0 triệu người, cao hơn 292,3 nghìn người, tương ứng tăng 0,6% so với quý trước và cao hơn 706,4 nghìn người, tương ứng tăng 1,4% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Trong đó, khu vực thành thị đạt 20,8 triệu người, cao hơn 140,2 nghìn người so với quý trước và cao hơn 491,2 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước; khu vực nông thôn đạt 32,1 triệu người, cao hơn 152,1 nghìn người và cao hơn 215,2 nghìn người. Xét theo khu vực kinh tế, lao động có việc làm quý III/2026 trong khu vực nông, lâm nghiệp và thủy sản là 13,3 triệu người (chiếm 25,1%), cao hơn 24,5 nghìn người so với quý trước và thấp hơn 38,0 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước; khu vực công nghiệp và xây dựng là 18,0 triệu người (chiếm 33,9%), cao hơn 150,0 nghìn người và cao hơn 394,1 nghìn người; khu vực dịch vụ là 21,7 triệu người (chiếm 41,0%), cao hơn 117,7 nghìn người và cao hơn 350,4 nghìn người. Hình 1 . Số người có việc làm phân theo khu vực kinh tếcác quý giai đoạn 2024-2026 Tính chung chín tháng năm 2026, lao động có việc làm đạt 52,7 triệu người, cao hơn 683,8 nghìn người (tương ứng tăng 1,3%) so với cùng kỳ năm 2025. Trong đó, lao động có việc làm khu vực thành thị đạt 20,7 triệu người, chiếm 39,3%; khu vực nông thôn đạt 32,0 triệu người, chiếm 60,7%. Xét theo khu vực kinh tế, lao động có việc làm chín tháng năm 2026 trong khu vực nông, lâm nghiệp và thủy sản là 13,3 triệu người, thấp hơn 147,7 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước; khu vực công nghiệp và xây dựng là 17,8 triệu người, cao hơn 447,4 nghìn người; khu vực dịch vụ là 21,6 triệu người, cao hơn 384,1 nghìn người. Tỷ lệ lao động có việc làm phi chính thức chung (bao gồm cả lao động làm việc trong hộ nông, lâm nghiệp và thủy sản) vẫn chiếm tỷ trọng lớn. Trong quý III/2026, tỷ lệ lao động có việc làm phi chính thức là 60,6%, thấp hơn 1,1 điểm phần trăm so với quý trước và thấp hơn 1,9 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Theo khu vực kinh tế, tỷ lệ lao động phi chính thức trong khu vực công nghiệp và xây dựng là 41,9%, khu vực dịch vụ là 52,7%, thấp hơn 1,4 điểm phần trăm so với quý trước ở cả hai khu vực; trong khi khu vực nông nghiệp, lâm nghiệp và thủy sản không thay đổi, ở mức 98,7%. Tính chung chín tháng năm 2026, số lao động có việc làm phi chính thức là 32,4 triệu người, chiếm 61,5% tổng số lao động có việc làm, thấp hơn 2,0 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm 2025. Tỷ lệ lao động phi chính thức tiếp tục giảm, cho thấy cơ cấu việc làm tiếp tục chuyển biến theo hướng tích cực. Tuy nhiên, việc làm phi chính thức vẫn chiếm tỷ trọng lớn, nhất là trong khu vực nông, lâm nghiệp và thủy sản, cho thấy việc giảm tỷ lệ lao động phi chính thức và thúc đẩy việc làm chính thức, bền vững vẫn là một vấn đề cần tiếp tục được quan tâm. c) Thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động [1] Số người thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động quý III/2026 là 617,3 nghìn người, thấp hơn 144,2 nghìn người so với quý trước và thấp hơn 78,5 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tỷ lệ thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động quý III/2026 là 1,31%, thấp hơn 0,31 điểm phần trăm so với quý trước và thấp hơn 0,19 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Trong đó, khu vực thành thị là 0,67%; khu vực nông thôn là 1,74%. Hình 2. Số người và tỷ lệ thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động các quý giai đoạn 2024-2026 Tính chung chín tháng năm 2026, số người thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động là 721,3 nghìn người, thấp hơn 43,0 nghìn người so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tỷ lệ thiếu việc làm trong độ tuổi lao động là 1,53%, thấp hơn 0,12 điểm phần trăm so với cùng kỳ năm trước; trong đó tỷ lệ thiếu việc làm khu vực thành thị là 1,05%; khu vực nông thôn là 1,86%. d) Thu nhập bình quân của người lao động Thu nhập bình quân của người lao động quý III/2026 đạt 9,2 triệu đồng/tháng, cao hơn 215,5 nghìn đồng so với quý II/2026 và cao hơn 823,8 nghìn đồng (tương ứng tăng 9,9%) so với cùng kỳ năm 2025. Thu nhập bình quân của người lao động chín tháng năm 2026 đạt 9,1 triệu đồng/tháng, cao hơn 752,8 nghìn đồng (tương ứng tăng 9,1%) so với cùng kỳ năm trước. posts.text: Dow theory - Wikipedia. The Dow theory on stock price movement is the precursor to technical analysis and is also part of modern technical analysis. [ 1 ] The theory was derived from 255 editorials in The Wall Street Journal written by Charles H. Dow (1851–1902), journalist, founder and first editor of The Wall Street Journal and co-founder of Dow Jones & Company . [ 2 ] Following Dow's death, William Peter Hamilton , Robert Rhea and E. George Schaefer organized and collectively represented Dow theory, based on Dow's editorials. Dow himself never used the term Dow theory nor presented it as a trading system. The six basic tenets of Dow theory as summarized by Hamilton, Rhea, and Schaefer are described below. Alfred Cowles in a study in Econometrica in 1934 showed that trading based upon the editorial advice would have resulted in earning less than a buy-and-hold strategy using a well diversified portfolio . Cowles concluded that a buy-and-hold strategy produced 15.5% annualized returns from 1902 to 1929 while the Dow theory strategy produced annualized returns of 12%. After numerous studies supported Cowles over the following years, many academics stopped studying Dow theory believing Cowles's results were conclusive. In recent years Cowles' conclusions have been revisited. William Goetzmann, Stephen Brown, and Alok Kumar believe that Cowles' study was incomplete [ 8 ] [ 9 ] and that W.P. Hamilton's application of the Dow theory from 1902 to 1929 produced excess risk-adjusted returns. [ 10 ] Specifically, the study from Goetzman and Brown found the return of a buy-and-hold strategy was higher than that of a Dow theory portfolio by 2%, but the riskiness and volatility of the Dow theory portfolio was lower, so that the Dow theory portfolio produced higher risk-adjusted returns according to their study. [ 10 ]
